solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Might one pass with those standards kept up?

parts.note: flags kept up are flying
standards are flags, as are colours

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone can pass a test while keeping their standards high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' looks like moral principles, but it means flags; the whole clue also hints at the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing 'with flying colours' is the idiom for succeeding outstandingly, so one might pass with them.

clue.text: Wood terribly dry, then a water supplier on the way

parts.note: fir is a kind of wood

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of dry, then and a are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the timber is awfully dry before turning to a roadside water source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the anagram signalled by 'terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street hydrant supplies water to firefighters and stands by the roadside, so 'on the way' places it.

clue.text: Contrary to opinion, week appears, ultimately, a long time

indicators.note: ultimately points at the end of each of the five words before it, so their closing letters are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Against expectation, the week turns out to last a very long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' looks as if it applies only to 'appears', but it takes the last letter of every word from 'Contrary' to 'appears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang for a very long period, as in 'I haven't seen her for yonks'.

clue.text: Party in minutes ending in government — probable landslide?

indicators.note: in places the party inside the word for minutes

parts.note: the minutes of a meeting are its notes
Con is short for the Conservative Party

indicators.note: ending in asks for the final letter of government

explanation.surface: A political party is recorded in the minutes as the government falls, hinting at an overwhelming election win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is the Conservative Party, abbreviated Con, a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide victory is so one-sided that there was never any real contest.

clue.text: Native American people almost as tribal, oddly, in European country

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the people's name is dropped

parts.note: the Crow are a Native American people of Montana

indicators.note: oddly calls for the letters in odd positions of as tribal

explanation.surface: A Native American people, being somewhat tribal, turn up oddly in a European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CROW to CRO, and 'oddly' takes A, T, I, A from 'as tribal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country on the Adriatic coast in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: United team is in the driving seat, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for being in control is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to be in the driving seat is to be in control, that is, to lead

explanation.surface: A football team, a united side, is said to be in control of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' has a capital for disguise: Leeds United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds United is a football club, so Leeds alone serves as the team's short name.

clue.text: Kind of door finished twice?

definitions.meaning: an ... door is a garage door that swings ... the opening
... both mean finished, as in 'time is up' and 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: A question about a type of door being doubly completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and over each mean ended, and the phrase also names a tilting garage door style.

clue.text: Egyptian god, determined

definitions.meaning: ... (or Seth) is the Egyptian god of storms and disorder
... means resolute, as in '... on going'

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity described as resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Set is both the storm deity of Egyptian myth and an adjective for being resolved.

clue.text: Country where capital's neither opened nor closed

indicators.note: with no opening and no closing, the capital loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: Tirana is the capital of Albania

explanation.surface: A riddle about a country whose capital city is in some half-open state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened' and 'closed' suggest a door, but they mean the first and last letters, T and A, are removed from TIRANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in Western Asia.

clue.text: For example, Tommy and soldiers, those working together

parts.note: Tommy Cooper, the fez-wearing British comedian and magician, is one Cooper
soldiers are a caste of ants, so ants can stand for them

explanation.surface: Tommy and some soldiers are offered as examples of people who collaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' suggests a British private soldier, but here it is Tommy Cooper, a famous British comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooperants are those who cooperate, acting jointly towards a shared end.

clue.text: Tree trunk enthusiast

parts.note: a trunk is a large storage chest
a nut is a fanatic, as in 'fitness nut'

explanation.surface: A tree trunk is admired by a keen fan of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' seems to belong with 'Tree', but it is a storage box.
explanation.definitionFit: The chestnut is a broad-leaved tree bearing edible nuts.

clue.text: Brute force said to break good man

indicators.note: to break into means to enter, so the reordered letters go inside the saint

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a good man

indicators.note: to force something is to wrench it out of shape, so the letters of said are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brute force is said to break a good man's resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brute force' reads as one phrase; split it: 'Brute' is the definition and 'force' the anagram signal, with 'to break' placing the result inside the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist delights in inflicting cruelty, so a brute is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Redeeming quality in old batsman after keeper's job?

indicators.note: after puts the batsman's name following the keeper's work

parts.note: a goalkeeper's job is saving shots
W. G. Grace was the great Victorian English cricketer

explanation.surface: An old cricketer's redeeming feature appears once the keeper has done his work.
explanation.walkthrough: W. G. Grace was a famous English cricketer of the 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving grace is the one good feature that redeems something otherwise poor.

clue.text: Possibly, lewd queen worried doctor

parts.note: adult material is possibly lewd, as in 'adult films'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: A lewd queen troubles a medical doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is the verb meaning tamper with, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to tamper with or falsify it, which is what adulterating does.

clue.text: General claims as support for property transaction

indicators.note: claims means takes hold of, so the general's name wraps round as

parts.note: General Lee led the Confederate army in the American Civil War
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A general asserts that something serves as backing in a property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims' looks like 'asserts', but it means takes hold of, so the general's name goes round 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaseback is a deal where a property is sold and then rented back by the seller.

clue.text: Moving a lot, I'm one on the move!

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declares that they travel a great deal and are always on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like travel, matching 'on the move', but it means touching.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving scene stirs the feelings, so it is emotional in the sense of affecting.

clue.text: Two Georges taking a test

parts.note: George VI and George V were British kings, giving VI and V

explanation.surface: Two men called George are sitting an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Georges are kings, written with regnal numbers VI and V.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, especially for a university degree.

clue.text: Figures, slightly retrograde

indicators.note: retrograde means going backwards, so the phrase for slightly is reversed

parts.note: a tad means slightly

explanation.surface: Numbers showing a slight decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and statistics, so figures is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Instrument shaken roughly about, mine inspiring ridicule primarily

indicators.note: inspiring here means breathing in, so the jumbled letters take another letter inside
shaken roughly suggests a jumbling, so about and mine are rearranged
primarily takes only the first letter of ridicule

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is rattled about while mockery comes from the coal mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken roughly' turns ABOUT MINE into TAMBOUINE, and 'inspiring' takes in R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a hand-held percussion instrument with jingling metal discs.

clue.text: Device locating companion in part of New England

indicators.note: in places the companion inside the state

parts.note: Maine is one of the six New England states
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A gadget for tracking down a friend somewhere in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locating' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is a mechanical apparatus, so device fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Witness watching over, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., it is someone at a cricket Test match, where they watch overs being bowled

explanation.surface: A witness who keeps watch over something.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket; spectators 'at Test' watch overs.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to certify or witness formally, as in a signed declaration.

clue.text: Message lovely and short in the end

parts.note: twee means sweet or cute, often too much so

indicators.note: in the end points at the last letter of short

explanation.surface: A message that is charming and brief at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like the brevity of a social post but supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on the social network formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: Game played with associated board, cheat and get low grade

parts.note: to crib is to copy dishonestly
to bag is to obtain
E is a poor exam grade

explanation.surface: A board game played while someone cheats and scores poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by pegs on a dedicated cribbage board.

clue.text: Creature putting leg under twice

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the leg below twice

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat
the on side, or leg side, is a half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: An animal tucks a leg beneath itself twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bison is a large wild ox of North America and Europe.

clue.text: Animal seen moving around Pacific native

indicators.note: moving around means the letters are shifted about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An animal is spotted roaming near a Pacific islander.
explanation.definitionFit: A Melanesian is a native of Melanesia, the island group of the south-west Pacific.

clue.text: Take in tenants every so often

indicators.note: every so often means at intervals, so alternate letters of tenants are taken

explanation.surface: A landlord occasionally accommodates lodgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' suggests housing lodgers, but it means consume.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, which is taking it into the body.

clue.text: Fracture that's the same!

definitions.meaning: the card game cry made when two matching cards turn up

explanation.surface: Someone spots an identical fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: In the children's card game Snap, players shout the word when two matching cards appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is both a sudden break and the cry used to claim a matching pair.

clue.text: Marry and make a splash?

definitions.meaning: literally, a plunge into water makes a splash

explanation.surface: Getting wed and causing a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means committing boldly to something, classically to marriage; literally it is a dive.
